newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday, recovering from heavy losses earlier in the week, dealers said.

"The session opened with high supply of dollars and this trend continued during the whole day. The dollar rose sharply since the beginning of the week and investors were taking profits today," said Guy Levi a dealer at Bank Leumi.
The U.S. currency had risen sharply from a rate of 3.253 on Friday to 3.2900 on Wednesday.

"Despite the rise of the dollar this week, activity was mixed and the trend was not clear," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim. "The rumour is there were only a few big investors who converted shekels into dollars during the last few days. Those investors were not active today and the shekel recovered."

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2770 shekels against 3.2900 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6490 shekels against 3.6661 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9084 shekels per 100 yen against 2.9043 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.1012 shekels against 2.1082 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2700 shekels.
